quotes.text: A shared Wi-Fi password can travel. Someone can write it down forward it, reuse it on a personal device, or keep it after leaving the company. A device certificate gives each managed laptop or phone its own proof instead.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in plain terms why device certificates are safer than shared passwords.

quotes.text: Microsoft Cloud PKI keeps the certificate process, but shifts much of that machinery out of your server room and into the Microsoft Cloud.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise definition of what Cloud PKI changes compared to on-premises PKI.

quotes.text: A password only proves that someone knows the password. A certificate issued through CloudPKi connects access to a device that Intune knows and manages.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Contrasts password-based and device-based access in two clear sentences.

quotes.text: So where should a small business start? Begin with one problem, not a company-wide certificate rollout. Maybe your staff Wi-Fi still uses one shared password.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical recommendation to start Cloud PKI with a single concrete use case.

chapters.title: How a device gets a certificate

takeaways: Device certificates let managed laptops and phones prove they belong without shared Wi-Fi or VPN passwords.
Microsoft Cloud PKI moves the root and issuing certificate authorities into Intune, removing on-premises servers, NDES connectors and HSM hardware from the plan.
Cloud PKI only covers Intune-managed devices, so start with one use case, make sure the Wi-Fi, VPN or app trusts the certificate chain, and test renewal and revocation.
hook: Shared Wi-Fi passwords and repeated VPN logins are still common in small businesses, yet running a traditional certificate infrastructure is often too much work. This episode explains certificates and Microsoft Cloud PKI in plain language and shows IT admins how Intune can deliver, renew and revoke device certificates behind the scenes.
